TASK: an exhausted underside is derived from the world model and the scene's authored placements, with NO new declaration. YOU MAY EDIT ONLY: storygame/runtime/item_facts.py, the NEW file tests/test_underside_exhausted.py, and docs/markdown-story-authoring.md (one short passage). READ ALSO: tests/test_observation_prompt.py, tests/test_observation_mode.py, tests/test_seat_scope.py (how the observation prompt and the complete-scope CONSTRAINTS line are built and tested), storygame/runtime/item_facts.py methods `_observation_scope_is_empty` and `_section_user_prompt`, storygame/runtime/observation.py, storygame/story_package/models.py `ItemPlacement` (field `under`), storygame/runtime/world_model.py (how scene `item_placements` with `under: true` are placed), and worldkeeper's `World.relation`, `World.parent`, `World.contents`. DESIGN. A scene's `item_placements` can place an item UNDER a focus (e.g. `{parent: <focus>, under: true}`). The underside of a focus is exhausted when: an observation request has a focus; the current scene authored at least one item placement with that focus as parent and `under: true`; AND none of those items is currently placed under that focus (`world.parent(item) == focus and world.relation(item) == 'under'` is false for each), AND no entity at all is currently under the focus (relation 'under' with that parent). A still-hidden item that is still under the focus keeps the underside NOT exhausted. Add a provider method (next to `_observation_scope_is_empty`) that returns this, and in `_section_user_prompt` add one more CONSTRAINTS line when it is true, exactly `- Nothing else is under the <name>. Searching under the <name> finds nothing more.` where <name> is the focus's public name (as the existing scope line does). It is independent of `contents_complete` and of `context.required`: it may appear together with the existing 'Nothing is left in or under' line only if both conditions hold (then emit both, in that order). Do not render it when there is no focus, when the focus is not the parent of an authored under-placement, or when an item is still under the focus. TESTS in tests/test_underside_exhausted.py (no model call), with a SYNTHETIC second package that has no Kristin/truck/drawer vocabulary (for example an observatory: a telescope tray with a lens placed under it, `under: true`) AND the real data/stories/continuity-initiative package: (1) before the item moves, an observation request focused on the focus has NO underside line; (2) after the item is moved to the protagonist (a world-model move, as the engine does after a recovery), the line appears exactly once with the focus's name; (3) a request focused on a different entity (the workstation or the truck, the telescope mount) never gets it; (4) the item moved BACK under the focus makes the line disappear; (5) a scene with no under-placements never gets it; (6) the existing scene-seat / scope-line tests still pass unchanged. DOC: in docs/markdown-story-authoring.md next to the `under` placement description add at most 5 plain lines: when an item authored under a place is no longer there, the engine tells the narrator nothing more is under it; no extra declaration is needed. Also run the existing focused suites tests/test_observation_prompt.py tests/test_observation_mode.py tests/test_seat_scope.py tests/test_observation_context.py and report counts.

TASK: a typed marker for knowledge statements a character may not say aloud. YOU MAY EDIT ONLY: storygame/story_package/ (models and loader/exporter files only as far as the new field needs), storygame/runtime/knowledge.py, data/stories/continuity-initiative/knowledge.yaml (exactly one added line), the NEW file tests/test_voiceable_knowledge.py, and docs/markdown-story-authoring.md (one short passage). Never edit storygame/runtime/item_facts.py (another task owns it). READ ALSO: storygame/story_package/models.py `KnowledgeDefinition`, storygame/runtime/knowledge.py `KnowledgeProjector._established_for` and `project` (the `sayable_knowledge` slice), storygame/runtime/cloudflare.py where `sayable_knowledge` is printed as '<name> may say this aloud: <statement>' (around the `_speaker_contexts` code and the loop that appends it), storygame/runtime/narration_safety.py (`dialogue_grounding_not_sayable` validates dialogue against the same list), tests/test_knowledge_projection.py, tests/test_speaker_presence.py. DESIGN. Add an optional boolean `voiceable` (default True) to `KnowledgeDefinition`. A statement with `voiceable: false` is still established, still part of committed knowledge and still reaches the narrator as context, but is NEVER projected as `sayable_knowledge` for any speaker (so it is never printed as a 'may say this aloud' line and dialogue quoting it is not grounded). Implement it in `_established_for` only. Because the loader or markdown/package round trip may need to know the field, check how KnowledgeDefinition is loaded and serialized (knowledge.yaml loading, any exporter or schema listing, package hash) and keep it consistent; the default must leave every package that does not use the field byte-identical in any pinned hash or export. DATA. In data/stories/continuity-initiative/knowledge.yaml add `voiceable: false` to the knowledge item with id `k_sl_1a_b_r0` (statement 'Kristin finds Michelle's memory card taped beneath the drawer and pockets it.') and to NOTHING else. Do not touch the other protagonist-led statements; the story author decides those later. TESTS in tests/test_voiceable_knowledge.py (no model call), with a SYNTHETIC second package or an in-memory knowledge catalog with no Kristin vocabulary AND the real package: (1) default behaviour unchanged: an established statement without the field is sayable for a present speaker; (2) a `voiceable: false` statement that is established is absent from `sayable_knowledge` for every audience but is still in `committed_knowledge`; (3) with the real 1A package after the card is recovered and a present speaker (the patrol officer placed in the protagonist's area, as tests/test_speaker_presence.py does), the built narrator user prompt does NOT contain 'may say this aloud: Kristin finds Michelle' and DOES still contain the officer's other sayable line when one is established; (4) dialogue grounding: an NPC segment quoting the non-voiceable statement is rejected with `dialogue_grounding_not_sayable` while a quote of a voiceable statement is accepted (follow tests that already exercise that code); (5) the loader rejects a non-boolean `voiceable`; (6) the real package loads and exactly one knowledge item has `voiceable` False. DOC: in docs/markdown-story-authoring.md where knowledge statement fields are described add at most 6 plain lines for `voiceable: false`: use it for a statement that records what the player character did (so a present non-player character does not repeat it as speech); the default is true. Also run tests/test_knowledge_projection.py tests/test_speaker_presence.py tests/test_narration_safety.py tests/test_1a_witnessed_recovery.py and report counts.
